title: Capture path swallows failures, misreports cancellation, retries a non-idempotent call and leaves partial state

consumerGuidance.architecture: The gateway's CaptureAsync is not idempotent unless an idempotency key is supplied; the project's IPaymentGateway exposes an overload that accepts one. Order state and the ledger entry are written through separate stores with no ambient transaction.
consumerGuidance.notes: The established error contract is to return CaptureResult.Failed with a reason; callers surface that to the customer. Cancellation flows from request abort.

mustCite: the catch-all that logs and returns CaptureResult.Success
the caller that marks the order paid on that result
the consequence that a failed capture is recorded as a successful payment and the stack context is lost
the correction of returning CaptureResult.Failed with the reason, per the project's established contract
that OperationCanceledException is caught by the same catch-all
that a request abort therefore surfaces as a gateway decline
the consequence of misattributed declines in payment reporting and customer messaging
the correction of letting cancellation propagate or reporting it distinctly
the three-attempt retry loop around gateway CaptureAsync
that the call is made without the idempotency key overload the project's gateway provides
the consequence of double or triple charging when the first attempt timed out after the gateway had captured
the correction of passing a stable idempotency key or checking capture state before retrying
the order being saved as paid before the ledger entry is written, across two stores with no ambient transaction
the consequence that a ledger failure leaves an order marked paid with no ledger record and no compensation
a proportionate correction such as writing the ledger entry first, or recording a pending state the existing reconciliation can complete

forbiddenFindings.example: Requiring exceptions instead of the project's CaptureResult type, or the reverse.
Requiring a distributed transaction, saga framework or outbox library without reference to the project's existing reconciliation.
Objecting to the retry loop being a for loop or to the log message wording.

notes: Four distinct failure-and-consistency rules on one changed method. The idempotency-key overload exists in the project, which is what makes the retry finding concrete rather than theoretical.
